name: Leavo
summary: Team time-tracking, attendance and overtime banking with transparent per-user pricing and a 30-day free trial.
best_for: teams that want straightforward time-tracking, attendance and overtime banking with transparent per-user pricing
skip_if: you need a permanent free plan (this is a 30-day trial), or you're a tiny team where a shared spreadsheet already covers hours
honest_knock: The tidy per-user numbers are annual-billed, and it's priced per seat — every employee you track adds to the bill, with no volume break published (large teams are told to ask sales). And the “free” is a 30-day trial, not a permanent free tier: budget for the paid plan from day 31.

pricing.entry_price_terms: per user a month billed yearly
pricing.notes: (price re-verified 2026-08-17, 2026-10-07 and 2026-10-19 against leavo.com/en/pricing) (2026) 30-day free trial with unlimited members and no credit card (a trial, not a permanent free plan). Professional $2.50/user/mo billed yearly ($450 a year for 15 members) or $3/user/mo billed monthly, and adds unlimited features and overtime banking; Premium $4.17/user/mo billed yearly ($750 a year for 15 members) or $5/user/mo billed monthly. Priced per user; the page describes yearly billing as 2 months free. Plan changes take effect immediately and are prorated, and adding a member raises the subscription quantity automatically at a prorated charge. Professional and Premium can also be paid by bank transfer against a monthly invoice; volume pricing for large teams goes through sales.

cost_traps.label: Per-seat pricing
cost_traps.evidence: Professional $2.50/user/mo billed yearly ($450 a year for 15 members) or $3/user/mo billed monthly, and adds unlimited features and overtime banking; Premium $4.17/user/mo billed yearly ($750 a year for 15 members) or $5/user/mo billed monthly.

compare_with.name: Toggl
compare_with.why: Toggl is the established time-tracker with a genuinely free tier for small teams; Leavo leans into attendance and overtime banking — richer there, but per-seat and trial-only at the free end

claims.claim: 1 invitation will go out in your name.
claims.observed: The invitation switch was off while this message remained; the row was removed and export later showed not_invited for both test members.
claims.comparability: Leavo invitation-preview text is compared with the switch state and later not_invited rows, without claiming that the removed wizard row triggered mail.
claims.buying_consequence: The contradictory wizard message is a UX finding; no unwanted invitation is proven.

exit_test.what: Two members, one created manually and one imported without invitations.
exit_test.awkward: Turning off wizard invitations still left the text “1 invitation will go out”; we removed the row and added the team later. This is a UX finding, not evidence of an actual unwanted send. Separate Create and Import Members actions were used; the export says not_invited. Import required lowercase permanent and called Employee default. Employee Code was not mappable. Export omits email, employee code and hire date, so matching is by name only. No invitation role was preselected.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 31 October 2026 on the free trial: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We set up a workspace, added one made-up employee by hand and one by CSV import, without invitations, and exported the member list.
findings: The trial showed 30 days, with no card. The 7-step setup imports Dutch public holidays and sets 25 days of leave by default.
In the setup, 'send the invitations' was on by default. With the switch off, the note under it still said one invitation would go out, so we added nobody there.
In the member list you can choose 'Create' or 'Create & Invite'; the second is the main button. No role is preselected.
The CSV import rejected 'Permanent' and 'Employee', the words the form uses. It wanted 'permanent' in lower case and calls the role 'default'. Both were easy to fix in the preview.
The employee code column could not be mapped in the import.
The CSV export kept the names with accents and shows 'not_invited', but has no email or employee code. Professional is $3 per user a month.
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.
